## Viewer paraphrase (quote, do not edit)

> You test a single frozen regression test over past git commits and determine when the test changes from pass to fail on the previous git commit states.

## Facilitator follow-ups (verbatim)

**What does the product prove?**

> It identifies the earliest point in between git commit states that the regression test fails

**What doesn't it prove?**

> It doesn't prove the root cause of the regression test failure, it simply states where the regression first starts

**COMMIT_PROOF — do you understand what it is? What is it? Anything wrong with it?**

> COMMIT_PROOF is a evidence package that has information about the frozen regression test, the git commit where it was executed on, the results of the regression test and supporting evidence that will let developers verify the point in between commits that the regression test fails. A limitation of this would be how it depends entirely on the accuracy of the regression test itself. If the test itself is not accurate enough it may not expose certain bugs to failure, which COMMIT_PROOF cannot detect.

## PASS rationale

Mentions a frozen regression check replayed over past Git commits and locating PASS→FAIL — without claiming the product is “AI finds bugs by itself.” Correctly refuses root-cause claims and names witness/test accuracy as a limit of `COMMIT_PROOF`.

## Setup / stranger-run notes (DEMO-01 retention)

**Reported setup time:** ~5 minutes

**Exact commands the subject ran (as reported):**

```text
npm install -g pnpm
pnpm -v
pnpm install
pnpm run
pnpm build
pnpm fl judge-proof
```

**Mistakes / friction (verbatim):**

1. Accidentally tried running this with python by habit
2. Installed a completely unrelated package with the same name
3. `npm install` failed at the start because it expected pnpm to already be installed. Specific cmd error:

```text
C:\Users\drdar\Desktop\faultline>npm install

> @mizore66/faultline@0.1.3 prepare
> pnpm run build

'pnpm' is not recognized as an internal or external command,
operable program or batch file.

npm error code 1
npm error path C:\Users\drdar\Desktop\faultline
npm error command failed
npm error command C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe /d /s /c pnpm run build
```

**Open used after setup:** `judge-proof`

### Install takeaway (not a claim of Codespaces success)

Subject reached `judge-proof` on Windows after installing pnpm globally. The first failure mode is exactly “ran `npm install` before pnpm/Corepack was available,” which the pin README path (`corepack enable` then `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`) is meant to avoid. Retain this as stranger friction evidence; do not rewrite it into a Codespaces success.
